agent_notes: Revised after the reviewer's request: the BDB citation is gone from the חַסְדְּךָ note, which now cites Metzudat David on 86:13 and Malbim on 86:13, both in the packet.

STEPBible glosses חסד as 'covenant loyalty'; I keep that in the word gloss. The five English versions split between 'mercy' (KJV, BBE, Webster) and 'kindness/lovingkindness' (YLT, ASV), and none carries the covenant sense.

The commentators divide on the time and the place: Radak reads the deliverance as past rescue from enemies and Saul, or as the grave, Meiri as future, and Rashi and Metzudat David as Gehinnom (Rashi: the adulterers' place; Metzudat David: the pardon for Bathsheba). I keep the text's plain 'Sheol, the lowest' and mention these readings in the commentary without choosing among them.

agent_notes: The sign (אוֹת) is read by Rashi, Malbim and the Targum as a public vindication, linked to Solomon bringing the Ark into the Temple; Radak reads it as kingship. These are traditional attributions of the psalm to David and I left them to the commentary as traditions, not as claims about the text. The psalm heading in the Hebrew attributes it to David.

חָסִיד is disputed: KJV/Webster 'holy', ASV 'godly', YLT 'pious', BBE 'true to you'. I chose 'one loyal to you' / 'devoted' because the word is the covenant-loyalty adjective from חֶסֶד, not ritual holiness (that would be קָדוֹשׁ). Rashi and Meiri record the rabbinic discomfort with David calling himself חסיד; I cite only their words in the packet.

Qere/accent: Radak and Meiri note שָׁמְרָה is an imperative with a long qamets (like 'שמרה זאת לעולם', 1 Chr 29:18), not a perfect 'my soul has kept'. I follow them; Ibn Ezra lists the perfect reading as a minority view.
Meiri reads נפשי אשא as an offering (מנחה), Metzudat David as leaning on God; I kept the literal 'I lift up my life' and let the commentary mention the range.

agent_notes: אֲדֹנָי в буквальном слое передан как «Владыка мой», чтобы отличить его от יהוה (Господь, в буквальном слое — YHWH); в драматическом слое, как и в Синодальном, — «Господи».
בֶּן־אֲמָתֶךָ: Синодальный — «сын рабы Твоей»; в драматическом слое оставлено «рабыни», чтобы сохранить социальный смысл (рабыня, а не «раба» как слово без пола).
חָסִיד передан как «преданный» (Синодальный: «благочестив»). В комментарии объяснено, что это человек хеседа, а не «святой»; Синодальный выбор отмечен как вариант.
